title: Looking for 2–4 UK testers for a strategy-backtesting tool (free, no catch, honest feedback wanted)
author: DeliciousEquipment13
selftext:
Hi all — I've built a tool called Atlas Edge and I'm looking for 2–4 UK-based people to test it before any public launch.

**What it actually is:** a backtesting and automation platform. You connect your own IG or Trading 212 account, build your own strategy from a library of components (breakouts, trailing stops, filters, etc.), and the platform runs it through a genuinely rigorous statistical validation process — walk-forward testing, placebo controls, realistic cost modelling — before telling you honestly whether it holds up.

**What it isn't:** a signal service, an "AI trading bot," or anything promising guaranteed returns. It doesn't tell you what to trade. Most strategies people build (including my own, extensively) get correctly rejected — that's the tool working as intended, not a sales pitch gone wrong.

**Why I'm posting this:** I want people who aren't me actually using it, breaking it, and telling me honestly where it's confusing or annoying, before I open it up more broadly.

**What's in it for you:**

* Free access during this test phase
* Direct input into what gets built next
* A genuinely rigorous way to test your own trading ideas before risking real money on them

**Requirements:** UK resident, 18+, comfortable connecting a broker account (demo account is fine if you'd rather not use live).

If you're interested,  DM me and I'll send over the details.

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: The walk-forward setup sounds promising. One failure mode worth testing explicitly is feature and position leakage across folds, especially when trailing stops or rolling filters reuse state. A purge window between train and test periods could make the rejection reasons even more trustworthy; that is the kind of evidence Marx would benefit from too.

comments.author: AttitudeGrouchy33
comments.body:
The rejection part is the most important feature here, imo.

Most backtesting tools accidentally make people more confident. A good one should probably disappoint them a lot. If Atlas Edge can show *why* a strategy failed, not just that it failed, that becomes way more useful than another green/red equity curve.

One thing I'd test hard before widening access: make the rejection reasons very plain-English. Not just "failed walk-forward" but something like:

- only worked in one regime
- profit vanished after realistic costs
- too few trades to trust
- drawdown clustered in a way the user probably won't tolerate
- signal depends on data the strategy would not have had live

That last one is the killer. People will forgive a rejected strategy if the tool teaches them what was fake about it.
